title: wcwf-world-class-2000-world-heavyweight
label: Dan Bonez

won.source: the promotion's own Total Anarchy 2001 broadcast

how: Won the eight-man tournament's own final by pinfall over Jason Myers with the Boner, after champion Raymond Chandler vacated the title earlier the same card.
note: Still champion at the close of the promotion's own surviving documents (the promotion's next surviving post is a July 2001 audio-show notice, no card).

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-world-heavyweight
label: Raymond Chandler

won.source: Already billed World Champion at the start of the promotion's own held run (Saturday Storm, 6 Jan 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

how: Already champion when the promotion's own surviving documents begin.
note: Retained the title through Meltdown (a best-of-three-falls main event the champion himself stopped at one fall each) and a Wednesday Evening Confessions three-way ruled a no contest, then voluntarily vacated it at Total Anarchy 2001 to open an eight-man tournament for a successor.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-international-television
label: Jason Myers

won.source: the promotion's own Total Anarchy 2001 broadcast

how: Became champion by default: still in the ring awaiting his own turn in the promotion's invitational format, he was named champion after Nathaniel Duke was taken out by an explosion and unable to continue defending.
note: Still billed the International Television Champion later the same card, entering the World Heavyweight Championship tournament final. Still champion at the close of the promotion's own surviving documents.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-international-television
label: Nathaniel Duke

won.source: Already billed International Television Champion at the start of the promotion's own held run (Saturday Storm, 6 Jan 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

lost.source: the promotion's own Total Anarchy 2001 broadcast

how: Lost the title without a fall: an in-ring explosion left him unable to continue the promotion's own invitational defense format (defend against every man who calls for a shot, in succession) after he had already beaten his first challenger. (ended: lost-by-forfeit)
note: Retained the title in a three-way at Saturday Storm, by disqualification (interference by the Unibomber) over Raziel Lucifer at Wednesday Evening Confessions, and in a ladder match over Jason Myers at British Brawl.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-united-states
label: Raziel Lucifer & JT Savage

won.source: the promotion's own British Brawl broadcast

how: Won a four-corner match (also involving Alec Azel and Bobby McCann) by a simultaneous double pinfall; owner Dick Hart ruled both men joint champions for one week pending a decider match the promotion's own surviving documents do not carry.
note: Still billed joint champions at the close of the promotion's own surviving documents; the decider match promised for the promotion's next Storm broadcast is not among the documents the promotion's own surviving record holds.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-united-states
label: Insane Cain

won.source: Already billed United States (Heavyweight) Champion at the start of the promotion's own held run (Saturday Storm, 6 Jan 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

lost.source: Owner Dick Hart announced the title's own reinstatement at the start of Wednesday Evening Confessions (11 Feb 2001), implying a vacancy the promotion's own surviving documents do not otherwise narrate.

how: Retained the title by submission over Derek Frost at Saturday Storm; how it went vacant afterward is not narrated in the promotion's own surviving documents.
note: A missing-shows gap: no document in the surviving record shows how or when the title left Insane Cain's hands.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-us-tag-team
label: Derek Frost & Shawn

won.source: the promotion's own Total Anarchy 2001 broadcast

how: Won the reinstated title from Cold Steel (Bobby McCann and Dante Reid) by pinfall, Shawn hitting Shawn's Swanton on Dante Reid.
note: The belts' own prior history is not narrated in the promotion's own surviving documents beyond their being 'retired' before this match. Still champions at the close of the promotion's own surviving documents.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-tag-team
label: Derek Frost & Shawn

won.source: the promotion's own British Brawl broadcast

how: Won the title from Salaok and Quartz's True Evil by pinfall, Shawn hitting the Shawnton Bomb on Quartz.
note: Still champions at the close of the promotion's own surviving documents.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-tag-team
label: Raymond Chandler & Jackson Therapy

won.source: Already billed World Tag Team Champions at the start of the promotion's own held run (Meltdown, 31 Jan 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

lost.source: Salaok and Quartz's True Evil are already billed 'the current tag-team champions' by British Brawl (8 Mar 2001); no title-losing document survives in the surviving record.

how: Not narrated in the promotion's own surviving documents; the change from Chandler and Therapy to True Evil happened off the held record between 31 Jan and 8 Mar 2001.
note: A missing-shows gap between Meltdown and British Brawl.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-tag-team
label: Salaok & Quartz

won.source: Already billed 'the current tag-team champions' at the start of the British Brawl broadcast (8 Mar 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

lost.source: the promotion's own British Brawl broadcast

how: Lost to Derek Frost and Shawn's YB2K1 by pinfall, Shawn hitting the Shawnton Bomb on Quartz, after Raymond Chandler ran in to even the odds when Nathaniel Duke took Derek Frost out of the match. (ended: lost-by-pinfall)
note: A missing-shows gap precedes this reign; how the title reached Salaok and Quartz is not narrated in the promotion's own surviving documents.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-texas
label: Jesse Helms

won.source: the promotion's own British Brawl broadcast

how: Won a six-pack elimination match (also involving Drake Lowen, Justin Marks, Eyval, Johnny Pyro and Cryptic) billed for 'the WCWF's newest Texas Title', pinning Johnny Pyro last with the Stoneshot.
note: Unresolved against the r001 reign above: Total Anarchy 2001, a document dated three weeks later, still bills Ric Landell the reigning Texas Champion. Neither document narrates the other; both are recorded as the promotion's own surviving documents state them.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-texas
label: Ric Landell

won.source: Already billed the reigning Texas Champion at Total Anarchy 2001 (31 Mar 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

how: Retained the title (undefeated in the match itself) despite Craven Blood winning a triple threat also involving Blaze by disqualification, because Landell himself was never pinned.
note: Unresolved against the r002 reign below: British Brawl (8 Mar 2001), a document dated three weeks earlier, bills Jesse Helms winning a separate, newly introduced Texas Championship. Neither document narrates the other; both are recorded as the promotion's own surviving documents state them.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-hardcore
label: Dane Rennier

won.source: the promotion's own Saturday Storm broadcast

how: Became champion in a multi-stage brawl also involving Ric Landell and Redneck Punk; the broadcast narrates the surrounding chaos in detail but never states the finish itself.
note: Still billed the Hardcore Champion at Meltdown (31 Jan 2001), the last mention of the title in the promotion's own surviving documents.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-cruiserweight
label: Eugene Whifflebottom

won.source: Already billed Cruiserweight Champion at the start of the promotion's own held run (Saturday Storm, 6 Jan 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

lost.source: Shawn is already billed 'current holder of the Cruiserweight title' by Meltdown (31 Jan 2001); no title-losing document survives in the surviving record.

how: Retained the title by submission over Psycho at Saturday Storm; how it passed to Shawn afterward is not narrated in the promotion's own surviving documents.
note: A missing-shows gap between Saturday Storm and Meltdown.

title: wcwf-world-class-2000-cruiserweight
label: Shawn

won.source: Already billed 'current holder of the Cruiserweight title' at Meltdown (31 Jan 2001); no title-winning document survives in the surviving record.

how: Not narrated; the belt passed to Shawn off the held record between Saturday Storm and Meltdown.
note: Billed the Cruiserweight Champion at Meltdown and Wednesday Evening Confessions, and once, at Total Anarchy 2001, billed instead 'the current WCWF lightweight champion' -- almost certainly the same belt named inconsistently by the promotion's own broadcast rather than a second title, but recorded here as the documents state it rather than silently corrected. Still champion at the close of the promotion's own surviving documents.
